    Inter Milan U19: Team Analysis – MH

    📅 05 Mar 2025 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2127 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 05.03.2025 in den Kategorien Team Portraits mit 0 Kommentaren.
    • Industry observers note that inter Milan’s U19 team is the only side in this season’s UEFA Youth League to have won all their matches so far, finishing the group stage of the “Youth Champions League” in first place.
    • Inter Milan generally builds up in a nominal 4-3-3 shape.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 05.03.2025 in den Kategorien Team Portraits mit 0 Kommentaren.

    Industry observers note that inter Milan’s U19 team is the only side in this season’s UEFA Youth League to have won all their matches so far, finishing the group stage of the “Youth Champions League” in first place. They also secured victory in the knockout playoff round and will now face Bayern Munich U19 in the Round of 16. This analysis will take a closer look at Inter Milan’s tactical structures and mechanisms under head coach Andrea Zanchetta in the Youth League while also considering possible approaches against them.

    Inter Milan generally builds up in a nominal 4-3-3 shape. A key role is played by the midfield trio, consisting of the two number eights, Topalovic and Venturini, alongside the single pivot, Mattia Zanchetta. Zanchetta frequently drops between the center-backs, taking on a key role in deep buildup, while the two eights serve as connectors and overload players in the transition from deeper buildup into more advanced areas. According to the Italian Wikipedia, head coach Andrea Zanchetta is the father of Mattia Zanchetta.

    According to recent reports, inter’s defensive structure varies depending on the opponent and pressing height. In mid-block and high-pressing phases, they defend in a narrow 4-3-2-1, a compact 4-3-3, or a 4-4-2, depending on the opposition’s structure. When defending deeper, they shift into a 4-1-4-1, with Zanchetta holding his position as the single pivot shielding the backline.

    As the central striker, either Lavelli or Spinaccè leads the line. Since both share a similar physical, robust playing style, this analysis will primarily refer to Spinaccè, who has started in recent matches. On the right wing, Pieri is a fixed starter, known for his strong 1v1 abilities. On the opposite flank, head coach Zanchetta has rotated more frequently, but he has consistently relied on technically strong, dribble-oriented wingers.

    Industry observers note that to build up against high pressing, Inter relies on certain patterns that make it more difficult for the opponent to press successfully. A frequent observation is that the center-backs move wide while the full-backs push up along the touchline. At the same time, the single pivot Zanchetta and/or the number eight Topalovic drop deep to lure the opposition’s midfield out of the center. The longer the possession phase lasts near their own penalty area, the more likely it is that both the pivot and the number eight drop into the center-back positions. The now-vacated central space is occupied by the other number eight, Venturini, and the frequently dropping center-forward Spinaccè. When buildup occurs on the right side, Topalovic often stays on the far side to stretch the central area further. The wingers act as additional passing options by tucking into the half-spaces. From this structure, the opponent can be bypassed using vertical-layoff combinations in the half-space.

    The primary goal of the buildup is often a pass to the target man Spinaccè, who either uses Venturini as a layoff option or directly switches play to the wing. By pulling apart the central space through the movements of Topalovic and Zanchetta, the goalkeeper typically initiates buildup through the wide center-backs, who frequently play a direct pass to the dropping striker via the now-open diagonal deep passing lane. Particularly noteworthy are the anticipatory movements of the layoff options in these combinations. The attacking number eight, Venturini, excels at positioning himself to receive layoffs from the back-to-goal striker Spinaccè, ensuring continuity in progression.

    Sources indicate that if only Zanchetta drops between the center-backs to form the resulting back three, the left-sided number eight, Topalovic, and the right-sided number eight, Venturini, move into the half-spaces to receive when the center-backs are in possession. Through a vertical-layoff combination involving one of the eights, the now-advancing pivot Zanchetta, and the dropping center-forward Spinaccè, the midfield can be quickly bypassed, allowing the ball to be switched to the wing in the opponent’s half.

    To effectively press Inter’s buildup directly, a hybrid pressing approach combining man- and space-orientation could be a viable strategy. A particularly crucial role could be assigned to the ball-far holding midfielder, who could operate positionally to close passing lanes, preventing deep balls into the target man Spinaccè while also ensuring that the central space cannot be stretched. Additionally, an aggressive step-out from a center-back would be necessary to avoid numerical inferiority in midfield. On the ball-near side, increased pressure could be applied through man-oriented marking to maximize pressing intensity.

    Through hybrid pressing, the center can be occupied, and the typical passing lane can be blocked. The downside is the numerical disadvantage on the ball-far side and the man-to-man marking on the last line.

    According to recent reports, even against teams that press deeper, certain patterns can be observed in Inter Milan U19’s buildup. From their usual 4-3-3 structure with a single pivot and two number eights, they transition into a three-man buildup shape against opponents using a two-striker system. To achieve this, Zanchetta drops between the center-backs, who move wider, while the full-backs push higher along the touchline. However, Zanchetta plays a flexible role, shifting between a central center-back position and his original pivot role, making himself available in midfield depending on the situation.

    This three-man buildup creates new passing connections designed to pose problems for the opponent. A key role is played by Topalovic and Venturini, who drop closer to the buildup to fill the emerging gap between the midfield and the first buildup line. The buildup is primarily conducted through the half-spaces and the wide areas. The ball-near number eight moves into the half-space to overload it, while Venturini, from the right half-space, moves into an advanced position, and Topalovic, from the left half-space, stays closer to the buildup zone, occasionally even dropping into the first line. The ball-far number eight occupies the center.

    Due to this asymmetry between the two eights, the wingers on each side have slightly different roles. On the right side, where Venturini often occupies the advanced half-space, the right winger stays wider, creating double width with the full-back. On the left side, since Topalovic supports deeper in the buildup, the left winger frequently moves into the half-space, opening the lane for the overlapping full-back on the outside.

    Additionally, Spinaccè overloads the half-space by shifting ball-near and dropping deeper. Particularly on the left side, a diagonal deep pass from the wide-positioned center-back in the back three can find either the winger or the striker in a diagonal alignment. This escadinha staggering provides multiple layoff options. The ultimate goal after playing through the half-space is to create a 1v1 situation on the wing, allowing the dribbling-strong wingers or advancing full-backs to be isolated and attack down the flank.

    Through the typical half-space overload, the wide area can be opened for a 1v1 situation involving the advancing full-back.

    Sources indicate that the follow-up action is usually a cross into the penalty area. This is typically occupied by the aerially strong striker, the ball-far winger, and Topalovic. In the second line, Zanchetta and Venturini can win second balls.

    One of the key aspects of Inter Milan’s game is their man-marking high press. With the exception of the match against Manchester City, coach Zanchetta’s team has consistently relied on man-marking and aggressive pressing in advanced areas. This approach frequently creates dangerous transition moments by forcing early turnovers.

    Sources indicate that while striker Spinaccè and the right winger are primarily responsible for initiating the press, Topalovic and Zanchetta operate in central areas. Zanchetta, known for his strength in duels, pushes far forward from his usual deeper pivot position to press opposing midfielders and win the ball in central areas. The offensively oriented number eight, Venturini, is deliberately kept out of direct 1v1 defensive duels in the center and instead takes responsibility for a potentially advancing full-back. On the opposite side, the opposing full-back is covered by Inter’s winger.

    According to recent reports, the pressing is almost always triggered by Spinaccè from a slightly left-sided position. He presses the goalkeeper while blocking the passing lane to the left center-back. This forces the opponent’s buildup toward the wing, where Inter engages in their man-oriented pressing. In particular, the ball-far midfielder, Topalovic, often abandons his direct man-marking after the opponent is forced to play toward the far-side wing. Instead, he drops back toward the defensive line to create numerical superiority and ensure that the center-backs can step out aggressively without leaving gaps in the last line.

    A possible solution against this man-marking press could involve putting the opposing center-backs in a dilemma. By having the strikers drop deep, they could force the center-backs to abandon their cover in the last line. Since Inter Milan’s full-backs are less dominant in defensive 1v1 situations, wingers making deep diagonal runs into the vacated spaces could create a favorable scenario. Once the press is triggered, these wingers should be played into 1v1 situations through deep passes. This either forces the physically strong center-backs out of the last line or creates a numerical superiority in midfield that can be exploited.

    Sources indicate that another possible approach could involve a high-positioned, inverted left-back. By dropping into the space between the opponent’s forward and midfield lines, he could create a central 1v1 against Venturini, who is not as defensively strong.

    Depending on the opponent, Inter may drop slightly deeper and defend in a 4-3-3 or 4-4-2 mid-block shape. This adjustment depends on the opposition’s buildup structure. The fundamental goal is to maintain numerical parity against the opponent’s buildup line, allowing Inter to transition into aggressive man-marking and press forward. Against a three-man buildup, they press in a 4-3-3 shape, while against a four-man buildup, they shift into a 4-4-2. A key emphasis is placed on central compactness, making it more difficult for the opponent to progress through the middle.

    Industry observers note that once the ball is shifted to one side, Inter looks to apply pressure and enforce man-marking, similar to their approach in the high press. Zanchetta frequently pushes forward aggressively on the ball-near side to put pressure on the opponent’s central midfielders and create ball-winning opportunities.

    While the full-backs also push high to apply pressure, the center-backs primarily serve as defensive cover. However, when the opposition’s strikers drop deeper, the center-backs do not follow them to avoid leaving gaps in the defensive line. Instead, Inter presses with one less player in the first line to compensate for the opponent’s numerical superiority in midfield. Even in these situations, the opponent is guided toward one side, where Inter then looks to regain possession. To execute this, the first pressing line must initially cut off the passing lane to one of the defenders, allowing the opponent to maintain more possession and reducing Inter’s ability to transition into their man-marking press.

    Especially in the low block, Inter Milan manages to make the field so compact that progression becomes extremely difficult. From a 4-1-4-1 structure, they compress the space just in front of their own penalty area. Zanchetta operates between the lines as a space-oriented pivot in front of the defense. When the opponent shifts play to one side, Zanchetta also moves laterally and looks to engage an opposing player.

    Recent findings suggest that as the central players shift heavily toward the ball side, defensive numerical superiority is often created near the ball, allowing Inter to apply pressure. The ball-far number eight secures the central area, while the ball-far winger stays wide when the opponent maintains width on both flanks to prevent switches of play. This enables the last defensive line to shift further toward the ball side, allowing the ball-near center-back to step out aggressively while still being covered.

    In a recent development, inter Milan’s U19 team manages to challenge opponents through a well-organized and versatile defensive structure. They can adapt to various pressing heights, with their difficult-to-play man-marking high press frequently creating dangerous transition moments close to the opponent’s goal.

    Sources indicate that in possession, Inter also succeeds in reaching the opponent’s penalty area frequently through a very direct approach aimed at attacking depth. The key to this is a well-coordinated midfield and a striker who can act as a target player, holding up the ball with his back to goal. Most of Inter’s combinations are designed to create a 1v1 situation on the wing, where both the advancing full-backs and the wingers are very difficult to defend.

    In 67 outings last season for Arizona, Loáisiga pitched to a 2.42 ERA, 1.03 WHIP and had 48 strikeouts in 67 innings.

    It has been revealed that the Yankees have re-signed left-handed reliever Tim Hill to a one-year, $2.25 million deal with a $2.5 million club option for 2028, per ESPN.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that this Friday, Nov. 20, is an crucial date on MLB's offseason calendar. It is the deadline for teams to offer 2027 contracts to their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players. The player does not have to sign by Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline, but he must be offered a contract. If he's not, the player is considered non-tendered and immediately becomes a free agent.

    Dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary. Adolis García, Nathaniel Lowe, Alek Manoah, and Christopher Morel were among the notable non-tenders last offseason. Go back a few years and substantial names like Cody Bellinger and Kyle Schwarber were non-tendered.

    With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors. You can be sure these teams will scour the trade market for these players and try to get something back before making the non-tender official.

    Projected salary: $11.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Duran was a non-tender candidate even before the Jake Bauers signing pushed him out of the everyday lineup. There is no such thing as too many good players, but the Red Sox now have two first basemen (Bauers and Willson Contreras) and four outfielders (Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela). Mickey Gasper and Masataka Yoshida are still around too. That's eight players for five lineup spots (first base, DH, three outfield spots). On any given day, three of those guys will be on the bench. Duran, who got MVP votes in 2024, had a 20-20 season in 2026, but it came with a ballooning strikeout rate and a .266 on-base percentage. He has been on the trade block for close to two years now and the writing is on the wall. If the Red Sox are unable to trade Duran this week, there's a real chance he'll get non-tendered Friday given his hefty salary projection.

    Projected salary: $7.7 million (team control through 2028).

    Former No. 1 overall draft picks have been non-tendered in the past (Tim Beckham most recently), just not by the team that drafted them. Non-tendering Torkelson would be a tough look for the Tigers even though he has not developed into the impact hitter he was projected to be coming out of Arizona State. Simply put, the salary is beginning to outweigh the production. Torkelson, 27, is a 25-30 homer bat with one of the league's highest strikeout rates, middling on-base percentages, and no secondary value (defense, baserunning, etc.). That said, the Tigers do not have an obvious replacement first baseman ready to step in (Colt Keith was the backup in 2026). That, plus the fact that Torkelson has No. 1 pick pedigree, could keep him in Detroit another year.

    Projected salary: $2.3 million (team control through 2029).

    Sources indicate that the American League Rookie of the Year in 2024, Gil has battled injuries and ineffectiveness in the two seasons since. The swing-and-miss rate on his fastball went from an elite 28.5% in 2024 to a below-average 18.8% in 2025 and 17.4% in 2026. Gil, 28, spent time in Triple-A this past season and the Yankees moved him into the bullpen late in the year, where the results were so-so. The salary projection is a pittance, particularly for a team with Upcoming York's payroll, though Gil is now out of minor-league options (he must pass through waivers to go to Triple-A) and doesn't have an obvious role. Because he is a pitcher and breathing, and also has a major award win in the not-too-distant past, the Yankees might be able to find a trade partner this week. If not, Gil is a definite non-tender candidate.

    Projected salary: $7.6 million (team control through 2028).

    A fan favorite and an All-Star this past season, Clement crashed hard in the second half, and the fact of the matter is he has a .295 on-base percentage in his three full seasons with the Blue Jays. Also, the soon-to-be 31-year-old's defensive numbers tumbled this year. Clement's contact skills are elite and he's a versatile, high-energy player. As a utility guy, he's an ace. As an everyday player, he's stretched. Clement's projected salary is hefty for a utility player, particularly one with limited offensive upside who no longer reliably catches the baseball. My guess is the Blue Jays will keep him and live with the salary, but it's not an obvious decision.

    Projected salary: $5.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Sources indicate that similar to Torkelson, non-tendering a former No. 1 overall pick would be a tough look for the Twins, but a clean break might be best for all involved at this point. Lewis, 27, has trended down since his boffo second half in 2023, enough that he was sent to Triple-A for a spell this summer. He's also moved down the defensive spectrum from third base to first base. It's not due to a lack of effort; Lewis is a major tinkerer who has tried all sorts of swing adjustments. It just hasn't come together. A fresh start elsewhere, away from the spotlight of former No. 1 pick and face of the franchise, might be best for him. The budget-conscious Twins could then reallocate the projected $5.1 million elsewhere on the roster. Right now, they can't count on Lewis to hit or have a meaningful impact defensively.

    Projected salary: $3.4 million (team control through 2028).

    It has been revealed that in 2023, Gorman slugged 27 home runs and looked like one of baseball's top young power hitters. In the three seasons since, he has not come close to repeating that success. The hope was that moving him to third base, his natural position, would unlock Gorman's offense following the Nolan Arenado trade. That didn't happen, and Gorman spent a major chunk of the summer in Triple-A, where he continued to have a hard time making contact. Now 26, Gorman has a minor-league option remaining and can go to Triple-A again in 2027, but the signs are not subtle. The Cardinals are reportedly seeking a stopgap third baseman until top prospect Jesús Báez is ready, which would likely not be the case if they had any belief in Gorman. That projected $3.4 million salary is a high price for a reclamation project ticketed for the minors.

    Projected salary: $6.9 million (team control through 2028).

    Right-handed power is in short supply throughout baseball and Burger, 31 in April, has hit at least 28 home runs in three of the last four years. He is a one-tool player, though. The home runs come with low batting averages, low on-base percentages, higher-than-average strikeout rates, and little to no defensive or baserunning value. Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young said his team lacked "grit and toughness," whatever that means, and indicated he wants more hitters who grind out at-bats. That's not Burger, who can hit the ball a mile but is not known for making life tough on pitchers. The $6.9 million projection could be deemed too pricey for a player with such a limited skill set.

    Projected salary: $6.6 million (team control through 2027).

    According to recent reports, doval went from the Yankees to the Pirates at the trade deadline, then from the Pirates to the Giants on waivers in September. He's a former All-Star who led the National League in saves in 2023, two things that have boosted his arbitration salaries. Since 2023, Doval has been a middle reliever who was on the outside of the Circle of Trust™ more often than not. The 29-year-old righty still throws very hard. There's nothing wrong with his arm. It's hard to believe he gets hit as hard as he does sometimes. Doval earned $6.1 million in 2026 and a player cannot have a salary cut by more than 20% during his team control years. That would set Doval's minimum 2027 salary at $4.88 million. I wonder if the Giants would offer him a pay cut, say $5.5M or so, and tell him it's either that or a non-tender. That happens a few times a year around the league.

    Projected salary: $6.5 million (team control through 2027).

    A fan favorite in San Diego -- "Ho-ly Sheets!" chants are commonplace during his at-bats at Petco Park -- Sheets has fallen by the wayside a bit with the Padres, so much so that he started just one of their six postseason games this year. The 30-year-old is a platoon player who is good against righties more than great and is a defensive liability at both first base and left field. Realistically, Sheets is a platoon DH, and teams rarely pay well for that role unless they're confident they will get big offensive numbers. In the grand scheme of things, the projected $6.5 million isn't much. It is top-of-the-market dollars for this skill set, however.

    Projected salary: $1.4 million (team control through 2029).

    Two years ago, Blanco threw a no-hitter in his eighth career start. This year, he was so far out of the picture that he pitched once in Houston's last 12 games (two innings at the end of a 13-2 blowout), and the Astros opted to start Peter Lambert on two days' rest with a postseason spot on the line in Game 162. Blanco, who is older than you may realize (he turned 33 in August), returned from Tommy John surgery this summer and had a rough go of it. The pitching-needy Astros could send him to Triple-A next season, as he has a minor-league option remaining, but his stuff was diminished after surgery, and again, they didn't trust him late in the year. You would be surprised at how many cheap pitchers get non-tendered every year. Blanco could join them this week.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Buffalo Bills will honor another key member of their iconic 1990s team.
    • It has been revealed that reed, who starred in Buffalo from 1985-99, is the franchise's all-time career leader with 941 catches, 13,095 yards and 86 touchdowns.
    • Reed has joined former teammates Jim Kelly, Bruce Smith and Thurman Thomas as the fourth Bills player in the organization's history to have his jersey number retired.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Buffalo Bills will honor another key member of their iconic 1990s team. The franchise unveiled on Thursday night that it will retire Hall of Fame receiver Andre Reed's No. 83 during the 2027 season.

    It has been revealed that reed, who starred in Buffalo from 1985-99, is the franchise's all-time career leader with 941 catches, 13,095 yards and 86 touchdowns. He had an additional 85 catches for 1,229 yards and nine touchdowns in 17 playoff games.

    Reed has joined former teammates Jim Kelly, Bruce Smith and Thurman Thomas as the fourth Bills player in the organization's history to have his jersey number retired.

    Kelly, Thomas and Bills owner Terry Pegula surprised Reed with the news.

    “There’s no family like your football family.” Some special guests revealed up to One Bills Drive to surprise @Andre_Reed83 with the news. @JimKelly1212 | @thurmanthomas pic.twitter.com/LUDGDB0h8c.

    "Oh man, it's almost like the moment when we all got the call for him going into the Hall of Fame," Thomas said. "We knew that he deserved to be in the Hall of Fame, and it was kind of the same thing. One of the four guys that, when you mention the Bills, his name is always mentioned.

    Sources indicate that "You saw his work ethic when we were in training camp together for 12 years, like, yeah, that guy is special, and he was a big part of our run to try to win a Super Bowl here. There aren't too many people today that go over the middle as much as Andre Reed did back in the day. He took a lot of punishment, but he was always there for us.".

    Reed was an integral part of Buffalo's historic run of success during the 1990s. While they didn't win a Super Bowl, Buffalo made history by becoming the first (and last) team to play in four consecutive Super Bowls. Reed caught eight passes for 153 yards in Buffalo's third of four consecutive trips to the massive game.

    Recent findings suggest that about time. Andre Reed’s number should have already been retiredGlad the Bills are finally giving him his due. Best WR in team history pic.twitter.com/FWDroOn6a7 https://t.co/lVC62BJ2hU.

    According to recent reports, buffalo's run also included the largest come-from-behind win in playoff history. The Bills overcame a 35-3 deficit to defeat the Oilers in the 1992 wild card round. Reed caught three consecutive touchdowns during Buffalo's comeback.

    January 3, 1993° 1992 AFC WILD CARD °LARGEST COMEBACK IN #NFL POSTSEASON HISTORYThe Oilers take a 35-3 lead over the #Bills early in the third quarter.Buffalo claws all the way back to lead 38-35, but Houston ties it to force overtime.#BillsMafia prevails in OT, 41-38. pic.twitter.com/SrZn6jGsZf.

    Reed was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2014.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.
    • Sources indicate that the full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman.
    • Industry observers note that as a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.

    Sources indicate that the full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman. Newcomers to the ballot are in bold.

    Industry observers note that as a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class. Those who get at least 5% of the vote can remain on the ballot the following year, and so on, for a maximum of 10 voting cycles. Players who are on the ballot for 10 years without getting 75% of the vote, in addition to players not getting 5% of the vote, fall off the ballot in ensuing years, though that doesn't mean the doors to the Hall are permanently shut.

    The results will be announced on Jan. 19, with the induction set for Cooperstown over the summer.

    Here's everything else you need to know about the Baseball Hall of Fame this offseason.

    It has been revealed that as alluded to earlier, there are two different votes each offseason. The BBWAA vote is for former players who have been retired from Major League Baseball for at least five years. It's the most common method in mainstream Hall of Fame ballot discussions. When you hear stuff like "first-ballot Hall of Famer," it means via the BBWAA vote.

    Players who don't make it via the BBWAA vote can get extra chances via committees. That's how, for example, Jeff Kent made it last year. Formerly called the Veterans Committee, the Hall of Fame now uses Era Committees, which are divided into two categories: contemporary baseball (1980 to present) and classic (prior to 1980). The contemporary ballot is then split into two, one for players and one for non-players like umpires, executives, pioneers and managers.

    Sure enough, this time around, it is a non-player Contemporary Baseball Committee, which looks at "managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980.".

    Industry observers note that we'll dive further into this group as we get closer to the Dec. 6 vote.

    Giants legend Buster Posey joins the ballot, and he's one of those cases where I don't think a bunch of people need to delve deeply into his numbers. More than statistics, sometimes we get "feel" guys, as in, you just know he's a Hall of Famer. Posey qualifies there, I would think, for 75% of the electorate. We'll obviously do a deeper dive in the coming weeks, but even without the longevity component (Posey only played in parts of 12 MLB seasons), I think he's in.

    Sources indicate that as for the rest of the first-timers, the best case would be Jon Lester. Given the way a lot of similar starting pitchers have been treated in voting in recent years, my hunch is he'll be able to hang around on the ballot, but he has a major uphill battle in order to get in.

    Then you're looking at Brett Gardner, Ryan Zimmerman, Kyle Seager, the short peak of Jake Arrieta and relief work of Andrew Miller. Good players worth mentioning, of course, but they won't sniff the Hall and it seems likely all behind Posey and Lester are one-and-dones on this ballot, as they'll fall short of 5% of the vote.

    This is the sixth year for Alex Rodriguez on the ballot, which means it's the sixth time that I point out that we don't really need much time to go over his case. His numbers say he's one of the 10 best position players of all time, but his ties to PEDs are keeping him out to this point.

    He did rise from 37.1% of the vote in 2025 to 40% last time, a new high-water mark. The progress is too modest to believe it's trending toward him getting in, but the number this year is certainly worth watching. If he somehow makes a leap to the 50% range, a deeper conversation might be in order.

    While some voters don't mind sending in blank ballots to prove some sort of nebulous point, most impose limits on themselves. Whether it's the actual rule of 10 or some voters saying they'll only vote, for example, for a maximum of three players on any given ballot, relatively weak ballots can leave openings for the best players to show huge gains. With Carlos Beltràn and Andruw Jones getting in last year and only one strong first-year candidate, perhaps Chase Utley can benefit.

    Utley is only in his fourth year on the ballot, but he's already made significant gains:.

    He only needs to add 15.9 points after jumping nearly 20 last voting cycle. The situation is ripe for Utley to either get all the way in or get close enough to where he probably makes the Hall of Fame in 2028.

    In a recent development, some of us are pushing to lower the Hall of Fame standard on modern starting pitchers, given the decreases in workload and how it affects their career numbers. We might be making some headway, but it's still tough sledding. Here are the holdover starting pitchers and their standing:.

    According to recent reports, the bar for relievers to make the Hall of Fame is justly pretty high. We recently saw Billy Wagner make a late move and make it in his last try on the BBWAA ballot. Francisco Rodríguez has had four chances on the ballot and gotten between 7.8% and 11.8% of the vote thus far.

    K-Rod ranks sixth all time in saves and has good rate stats. He's worth tracking as it relates to three active relievers. Kenley Jansen is third in saves with a similar number of innings pitched to K-Rod. Craig Kimbrel is fifth and has more than 100 fewer innings pitched. Aroldis Chapman is ninth and in the ballpark of Kimbrel in workload to this point.

    According to recent reports, if K-Rod continues to have trouble making headway toward induction, does that mean Kimbrel and Chapman will have trouble as well? What about Jansen?

    Who else is back on the ballot? A quick look:.

    According to recent reports, posey is a lock. If the committee era chooses Bochy, Baker and/or Sabean, that would be some nice San Francisco flavor, too, right? I'll predict that committee ballot at a later date, though.

    I'll also say Utley's good roll here continues with a relatively weak ballot (at least when you factor in what the PED stain has done to some guys).

    On the player side, my 2027 Hall of Fame class prediction is Buster Posey and Chase Utley.

    #16025. Bengals duo could break NFL record that has stood for 31 years: Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on historic pace

    Bengals duo could break NFL record that has stood for 31 years: Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on historic pace

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (716 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • CINCINNATI -- The Cincinnati Bengals offense has been nearly unstoppable this year.
    • It has been revealed that through the first 10 weeks, there are only seven players in the NFL who have topped 800 receiving yards, and both Bengals players are on that list.
    • Chase and Higgins are just the fourth receiving duo in NFL history to both hit the 800-yard mark in just nine games (Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have also topped 800 yards this year, but the Packers duo has played 10 games compared to just nine for the Bengals duo).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    CINCINNATI -- The Cincinnati Bengals offense has been nearly unstoppable this year. Heading into Week 11, Joe Burrow is the MVP favorite and one of the reasons that he's been so successful this year is because he has arguably the top receiving tandem in the league in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

    It has been revealed that through the first 10 weeks, there are only seven players in the NFL who have topped 800 receiving yards, and both Bengals players are on that list. Chase ranks fourth in the NFL with 878 receiving yards while Higgins is right behind him with 824 yards, which ranks sixth in the league.

    Chase and Higgins are just the fourth receiving duo in NFL history to both hit the 800-yard mark in just nine games (Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have also topped 800 yards this year, but the Packers duo has played 10 games compared to just nine for the Bengals duo).

    The two Cincinnati receivers are both on pace to finish with more than 1,500 yards, which is mostly notable because no team has ever had TWO players hit 1,500 yards in the same season. As a matter of fact, it's been 26 years since a duo even came close to hitting that mark.

    Sources indicate that back in 2000, Torry Holt finished with 1,635 yards while playing for the "Greatest Show on Turf" Rams and his teammate, Isaac Bruce, finished with 1,471. In 1995, the Lions' receiving tandem of Herman Moore (1,686) and Brent Perriman (1,488) came closer than anyone to having two players on the same team hit 1,500 yards, but Perriman came up 12 yards short. The Lions duo totaled 3,174 yards, which is the NFL record for a receiving tandem. The record has somehow stood for 31 years, even with the league now in a pass-happy era.

    Recent findings suggest that this year, Chase is on pace for 1,658 yards while Higgins is on pace for 1,556, which would put them at 3,214, topping Moore and Perriman. During a press conference on Thursday, Chase was asked if it would be meaningful for him and Higgins to become the first duo to top 1,500 yards in the same season, and he didn't hesitate with his answer.

    "100%," Chase stated. "I'm not pushing for it, but I'm definitely speaking it into existence with me and Tee.".

    This week, the Bengals get to face a Commanders defense that has given up at least 120 receiving yards to five different players this season, so Chase and/or Higgins could end up having a major game on Monday night.

    Burrow is good at spreading the ball around, which is why Chase and Higgins are both succeeding.

    It has been revealed that both guys have been hot at different times this season. There was a four-game span starting in Week 4 where Higgins topped 145 yards in three of four games. As for Chase, he's been unstoppable over the Bengals' past three games, catching 32 passes for 527 yards. In terms of NFL history, Jerry Rice is the only player who's had a better three-game span and that happened back in 1995.

    One reason the Bengals' star duo is putting up such massive numbers is that opposing defenses can't seem to figure out who they should take out of the game.

    "What all that going on with me and Tee is just how the coverage works out," Chase said of why one of them always seems to be open. "Maybe a coverage could be sliding to my side the whole time, but then the coverage that's sliding to my side is the look we want or maybe it's the opposite, they're going to my side and it's not open, but Tee's getting a one-on-one on the backside. It's really pick your poison playing with us. And this year, Tee's jumped into more of a bigger role of his play than usually.".

    Recent findings suggest that chase and Higgins have both hit 1,000 yards in the same season twice, but that hasn't happened since 2022. Both guys could hit that number before the month of November is over, and if that happens, they'll have their sights set on the historic 1,500-yard mark that no duo has ever hit.

    It has been revealed that this season's NBA Rookie of the Year race has the potential to be one of the closest in league history. While there is no 65-game requirement to win the award — unlike MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and All-NBA honors — playing as many games as possible will be paramount this season in order to claim Rookie of the Year.

    Sources indicate that that's why Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson faces an uphill climb to win the honor after fracturing his right hand earlier this month. Wilson is set to miss the next 3-5 weeks and will likely lose serious ground to others in his class. He currently has the sixth-best odds (+4000) on FanDuel Sportsbook to win Rookie of the Year.

    It has been revealed that during the first month of the season, three players have separated themselves at the top: Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer, and Darius Acuff Jr. While it's not a guarantee one of those players wins it, if the season ended today, those would be the top vote-getters.

    Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa — the first two picks of the 2026 NBA Draft — have some ground to make up during the next four months to get back in the mix.

    With the regular season almost a quarter of the way complete, let's dive into our first Rookie of the Year rankings. All odds via FanDuel.

    According to recent reports, with Steph Curry out, Lendeborg has continued to step up. The oldest player drafted in the first round is coming off a lackluster showing against the Spurs in the NBA Cup, but before that he had three straight games of 23+ points. He is shooting 48.6% from the field and 41.4% from 3. Lendeborg didn't start shooting 3s on a consistent basis until he got to Michigan last season, so knocking down that percentage on 5.4 attempts per night is a positive sign. Fourteen games into the season, Lendeborg is the favorite.

    According to recent reports, boozer's raw stats aren't as good as Lendeborg's or even Acuff's, but his impact goes well beyond the box score. His feel for the game is elite for a 19-year-old. Boozer keeps getting better and better as a processor as he continues to log more minutes. The Grizzlies have been one of the league's surprising teams this season. Boozer deserves a ton of credit for that. He wins everywhere he goes, whether at the high school, college, or professional level.

    Acuff just turned 20 last week. In 13 games as a teenager, he averaged 25.5 points per game and became the first teenager in NBA history to score at least 275 points and dish out 80 assists in his first 11 games. Acuff is a special offensive talent who is being asked to do more than any rookie in his class. Sacramento is a very bad basketball team, but Acuff makes the Kings somewhat fun to watch. That's a huge credit to him.

    Recent findings suggest that the Jazz have been decimated by injuries this season and are right now riding a 12-game losing streak. The one bright side amidst some very bad basketball is how good Peterson has been during that stretch. Peterson had a five-game stretch in which he scored 20 points in each game and shot the ball well from 3. Peterson is the future of Utah's franchise, so getting him as many reps as possible on and off the ball should be the priority.

    Sources indicate that dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick, is averaging 14 shot attempts per game during his first 10 appearances as a pro. He should be taking even more shots. The way the Wizards are using him is confusing at times. Dybantsa is in somewhat of a weird situation because of the Wizards' roster. Washington handed Trae Young a huge contract this offseason that is already aging poorly. Dybantsa should be the focus of the offense. He should be touching the ball and shooting it even more than he is already. I have been impressed with Dybantsa's defense this season.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving.
    • As for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov.
    • It has been revealed that the Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving. In Major League Baseball, that usually means a slow news week. Those of us wanting a flurry of moves before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 are starting to lose a little hope, but hey, it's still possible. We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.

    As for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov. 16, let's go.

    It has been revealed that the Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson.

    Rogers is the best option here. He finished last season with a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts. CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 3 free agent this offseason and the best non-Tarik Skubal pitcher on the market. Here's part of the write-up:.

    Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.

    As things stand, the Orioles' rotation starts with right-handers Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Cade Povich is a left-handed option, but they'd clearly like someone else who could qualify as a frontline starter from the left-handed side.

    In a recent development, former Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara has been involved in trade rumors for years and the Marlins never end up moving him. More of the same this offseason? Probably.

    "I expect Sandy to be on the Marlins next year," general manager Peter Bendix told MLB Network.

    Alcantara, 31, was 13-11 with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153 strikeouts in an MLB-best 214 innings last season. He also grabbed three saves down the stretch as the Marlins started experimenting with using starters in relief on their bullpen day between starts. The 2022 Cy Young winner missed all of 2024 after having Tommy John surgery and started to show flashes of his old self last season. He's now making $21 million in 2027 before hitting free agency.

    If the Marlins contend, he'll surely stay put, but if they fall out of contention, it'll be another round of trade rumors.

    Sources indicate that free agent left-hander A.J. Minter is getting a lot of interest, per MLB Network. Coming off a season in which he was productive for both the Mets and Twins (in all, a 2.56 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 41 strikeouts in 45 ⅔ innings), he's being chased by at least the Blue Jays, Nationals, Phillies, Rangers and Royals.

    Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

    📅 31 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    It's vital to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    In a recent development, montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    According to recent reports, we already know the Wild are major-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    In a recent development, however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't presently have on their roster.

    According to recent reports, carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    In a recent development, similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    #16019. The Timing Game – MH

    📅 31 Mar 2025 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4148 w)
